finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the result, so the admin check is never enforced. Any authenticated user can run purgeAll(). This is a broken authorization (missing enforcement) flaw. rotateKeys uses mustPerm correctly, which shows the intended pattern.
finding.source: Any authenticated low-privilege user sending a request to the purge route. They do not need the admin permission.
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive admin-only operation.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the user from the request context.
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns a bool that is ignored. There is no early return and no 403 response.

finding.guards_checked: Only handlers.go exists, so there is no router or middleware to check. checkPerm only returns a bool and writes no response. The handler has no other permission check and does not use mustPerm. I could not verify the context middleware that sets userKey, so any route-level guard is unknown. Nothing in the handler enforces admin.

verdict.guard_found: none in handler: checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) returns a bool with no response/abort, and its result is discarded at line 26. No router or middleware exists in the directory. The unseen context middleware only sets the user and is not an admin guard.
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u, "admin") as a bare statement, so its bool is discarded, and purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any authenticated user. rotateKeys at handlers.go:33-35 shows the correct mustPerm pattern.
